newsitem.title: UK: Marine insurance rates still falling - expert.
newsitem.headline: Marine insurance rates still falling - expert.

text.p: Tough market conditions are pushing marine insurance rates lower, even though some underwriters are taking a firm line on bad risks, an industry expert told a conference on Friday.

Many prudent underwriters were making greater use of the word 'no' and had the confidence to let under-rated and sub-standard risks go elsewhere, Tony Nunn, adviser to the Institute of London Underwriters (ILU), said.
Nunn, who is governmental and international affairs adviser to the ILU, was speaking at a two-day conference arranged by Erasmus University in Rotterdam on safer shipping and cleaner oceans.

In the last 18 months much of the ground recovered by marine insurers to obtain adequate levels of premium had been lost and the current aggressive attitude of many international insurers persisted, he said.

"The opportunity for any further action by insurers in a free competitive market at present is limited due to the fact that there are so many underwriters worldwide writing business, so there is little likelihood of obtaining cohesive action."
Defining a sub-standard ship was not easy, Nunn said, but noted that basic management, ownership and shoreside management could often be as important as factors such as age or construction.
